name: Bright Light Green
lede: Bright Light Green stacks two modifiers onto [[green]]: bright for the saturation, light for the lightness.

sections.title: A double modifier
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar: bright plus light plus green, not a word anyone coined on its own [1]. The ISCC-NBS system filed a block of similarly brilliant yellowish greens in 1955 [1], and a 1930 Maerz and Paul plate already carried a close match, first recorded in 1922 [1]. The xkcd 2010 crowd color survey later gave the public name its final spelling [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[lighter-green]], a duller green only 3.4 units away [2]; [[bright-green]] is close too, and more vivid [2]. All three sit on the same yellow-green slice of the wheel, a family that also holds [[chartreuse]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries this exact green covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A color this saturated and this light is rare on an aged, varnished surface, whatever paintings may have once looked like unvarnished [3].

origin.named_after: its own saturation and lightness, stacked onto green
